results.notes: R047 is this simulant's only formal reference and could not be opened (paywalled; both attempted URLs returned 403). Because it is the actual primary source most other documents cite for Oshima's properties, all support here comes from secondary sources instead. Rich data found but not entered as new_values because units/format don't fit the DB schema: simulantdb.com (NEW3) mineralogy 'Basalt 85%, Ilmenite 8%, Forsterite 7%' is explicitly described as a manufacturing recipe ('Oshima... with slightly less added olivine' than FJS-3) — i.e. proportions of a rock (basalt) plus added minerals blended to make the product, not a measured mineral assemblage of the finished simulant, so per the ground rules this was not reported as mineral:<component> values (Basalt is a rock; even Ilmenite/Forsterite here represent recipe inputs, not lab-measured phases). Its bulk chemistry table is in ELEMENTAL wt% (Si 36.31, Ti 5.81, Al 11.71, Fe2+ 8.17, Fe3+ 14.42, Mg 7.42, Ca 12.15, Na 2.71, K 0.64, Mn 0.49, P 0.08, S 0.01, Total 100.00), not oxide wt%, so does not map onto 'oxide:<component>' fields without conversion (not performed). Mean grain size given as 88 μm (a mean, not the d50 median implied by 'particle_size_d50'). Documents that merely mention Oshima in passing lists and were not opened further: papers/LRS/DIRT project/files/1643/S2095268624001381.html; papers/LRS/DIRT project/files/1793/S294992912500052X.html; papers/LRS/1-s2.0-S2095268621001002-main.pdf and its duplicate content in .../files/1712/330911730_...NEU-1...html and papers/LRS/Li et al. - 2022 - Preparation and characterization... (lunar low gravity).pdf; Taylor et al. 2016 (papers/LRS/Taylor et al. - 2016 - Evaluations of lunar regolith simulants.pdf) reproduces the same LEAG-CAPTEM-derived table used for MKS-1 but does not add Oshima-specific detail beyond what's already captured via NEW1/NEW4.

problems: Minor location error. The sentence 'One example is the Kohyama base simulant, developed by the Shimizu Corporation in Japan' is on p.4, left column, at the end of the background section, just before the heading '3. Lunar regolith simulant system'. It is not inside Section 3. The Table 1 row on p.2 is correct.

I rendered p.63 (Table 9, Japan block) and confirmed the Kohyama row's Supply Confidence cell is red. The Key reads '= Previously produced, no/limited stockpiles exist'. The email 'uyama@shimz.co.jp' is in one merged Contact cell that covers all six Japan rows.

I fetched the page live on 2026-09-24. The .php URL redirects (301) to https://simulantdb.com/simulants/kohyama.html. After stripping tags, the live text is identical to the saved copy papers/agent-fetched/simulantdb_kohyama_2026-09-24.html.

The row is in 'Table 1 List of lunar mare soil simulants developed until Sep/30/2023' (Ruan et al. 2024, Acta Astronautica 224, 148-160). That is the paper's Table 1, not a table inside the Introduction. The paper also characterises a new simulant (IGG-01), so kind 'review' is inaccurate.

The row 'Kohyama Japan 2008 Gabbro Highlands & mare general use' in IGG-01 Table 1 (Year column) is verbatim. Other documents give 2008 only as the Sueyoshi et al. 2008 publication year (LEAG 2010 App. 4: 'Base stimulant, Sueuoshi et al, 2008'), not as an explicit release date.
simulantdb's 'Availability: May Be Available' is quoted correctly, and no document uses the literal phrase 'Limited Stock'.

There is partial support that the extractor did not follow up. ISECG 2021 Table 9 (p.63) colours Kohyama red: 'Previously produced, no/limited stockpiles exist'. The ESRIC knowledge portal copy (papers/LRS/DIRT project/files/1735/simulants.html; url http://knowledge.esric.lu/simulants/, saved 2025-03-03) says in text: 'Name Kohyama Base Simulant Description Average luna highland (general) Availability Previously produced, no/limited stockpiles exist Supplier/Contact Shimizu Corporation Japan'. NASA ARES (papers/LRS/DIRT project/files/1646/simulants.html; https://ares.jsc.nasa.gov/projects/simulants/, saved 2025-02-03) lists 'Kohyama Base Moon (Intermediate)' among Marshall Space Flight Center holdings 'as of 2017'.
'no/limited stockpiles' covers both none and limited, so it does not state 'Limited Stock' outright. A curator should decide whether to accept it.

The extractor says 'Highlands' matches no opened document, but its own NEW2 quote contains the support. ISECG 2021 Table 9, p.63: 'Kohyama Base Simulant   Crushed Gabbro from Kohyama (Japan) area   Average luna highland (general)'. The ESRIC portal (papers/LRS/DIRT project/files/1735/simulants.html) states the same: 'Kohyama Base Simulant Description Average luna highland (general)'.

So support for 'Highlands' exists. It conflicts with several sources that call Kohyama intermediate: LEAG-CAPTEM 2010 App. 4 p.85 'Between highlands and mare (general use)'; Taylor et al. 2016 Table 2 'Intermediate; highlands & mare'; Linke 2020 'intermediate'; simulantdb 'intermediate between highlands and mare'; IGG-01 'Highlands & mare'; NASA ARES 'Moon (Intermediate)'. The curator should resolve the conflict. It should not be marked as having no source.
The Linke 2020 p.4 quote is verbatim. ESRIC (files/1735/simulants.html) also names Shimizu explicitly: 'Supplier/Contact Shimizu Corporation Japan'.
